terms.comment: The word “thrown in between”. Traupman’s pupil defines it as pars ōrātiōnis significāns mentis affectum vōce inconditā, a part of speech showing a feeling by an inarticulate cry (237). In rhetoric the same word is a parenthesis (Quint. 8.2.15).

phrases.latin: noster sermō articulōs nōn dēsīderat … sed accēdit superiōribus interjectiō
phrases.english: our language does not need articles … but the interjection is added to the others

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 220, p. 237, p. 247.
